Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:11:1.hebrew: ולא תשלומי שלשה וארבעה - שלשה לשה וארבעה לשור, דכיון דאימעיט מכפל, בצר להו חדא, שהכפל בטובח ומוכר בכלל תשלומי ד' וה':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:11:1.english: But not payment of three and four [times] - Three [times] for a sheep and four [times] for an ox, for since it was excluded from double [payment], they are reduced by one, since the double [payment] in [the case of] one who slaughters or sells is included in the payment of four and five [times].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:12:1.hebrew: וכי יתן וגו' - לקמן בהשואל (בבא מציעא דף צד:) אמרינן: פרשה ראשונה נאמרה בשומר חנם, שניה בשומר שכר. וכתוב בפרשה ראשונה "ונקרב בעל הבית וגו'", ואוקימנא לשבועה בהמפקיד (לעיל בבא מציעא דף מא:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:12:1.english: And "When [a man] delivers," etc. - Later, in [the chapter] HaShoel (Bava Metzia 94b), we say [that] the first passage was stated regarding an unpaid bailee, [and] the second regarding a paid bailee. And it is written in the first passage, "then the master of the house shall approach [the judge], etc." (Exodus 22:7), and we established [this phrase] as referring to an oath in [the chapter] HaMafkid (above, Bava Metzia 41b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:18:1.english: Their shekels - The shekels of Adar for communal offerings.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:18:2.english: And they were stolen - From the agents.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:19:1.hebrew: אם משנתרמה התרומה - אם כשבאו לדין, כבר נתרמה התרומה, שהיו תורמין הלשכה בג' קופות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:19:1.english: If [this occurred] after the contributions had been collected - If, when they came to court, the contribution had already been collected, for they would collect [from] the [Temple] chamber in three baskets.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:2:1.hebrew: ואין רבית ואונאה להקדש - אין איסור אונאה ואיסור רבית נוהג בהקדש, ולקמיה מפרש היכי דמי רבית דהקדש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:2:1.english: And there is no interest or exploitation for consecrated [property] - The prohibition of exploitation and the prohibition of interest do not apply to consecrated [property], and later [the Gemara] explains what a case of interest regarding consecrated [property] is.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:2:2.english: The law of overcharging [applies] to a layman - [Namely,] one-sixth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:2:3.english: And the law of exploitation does not [apply] to consecrated property - For even [when it is] less than the threshold of exploitation, [the transaction] is rescinded.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:3:1.hebrew: היינו דקתני כו' - בתמיה, והא חומרא דהקדש הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:3:1.english: Is that what is taught, etc. - [This is asked] in astonishment: for this is a stringency of consecrated [property]!

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:3:2.hebrew: ומשני, כי קתני חומר דהדיוט, ארבית קאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:3:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: When [the baraita] teaches a stringency of a layman, it refers to interest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:3:3.english: With regard to exploitation - And on account of exploitation, let [the tanna] also teach: "This is the stringency [lit., fifth] with regard to consecrated [property]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:4:1.english: But [with regard to] consecrated [property], [is] this [its] stringency, and nothing further - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:5:1.english: That he lent - That he lent [it] to a layman.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:5:2.hebrew: והלא מעל - שהוציא מעות הקדש לחולין ולא הכניס תחתיהן להקדש כלום, ושוגג הוא אצלו, כסבור שמותר משום שכר הקדש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:5:2.english: And didn't [he] misuse [consecrated property] - For he removed consecrated money to non-sacred [use] and did not bring anything into the Temple treasury in its place; and he is [acting] unwittingly in this regard, as he thinks that it is permitted for the sake of profit for the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:5:3.hebrew: והוו ליה דהדיוט - של גזבר, שהרי עליו לשלם להקדש קרן וחומש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:5:3.english: And they become [the property] of a layman - [They belong] to the treasurer, for he must pay the principal and a fifth to the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:6:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן - האי דקתני אין רבית להקדש, לאו בהלואה קאי, אלא בהדיוט שקיבל מעות מן הלשכה, מן הגזבר, לספק סלתות כל השנה למנחות של צבור, ארבע סאין בסלע, והוקרו ועמדו משלש סאין בסלע. דאילו הדיוט, אסור לפסוק על פירות עד שיצא השער, וכאן, אפילו לא יצא השער עדיין, לארבע פוסקין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:6:1.english: With what are we dealing here - That which [the Mishnah] teaches, [that] there is no [prohibition of] interest for consecrated property, does not refer to a loan; rather, [it refers] to a private individual who received money from the [Temple] chamber, from the treasurer, to supply fine flour [throughout] the entire year for the communal meal-offerings [at] four se’a per sela, and they rose in price and stood at three se’a per sela. For whereas [for] a private individual it is forbidden to contract for produce until the market price has gone out, here, even if the market price has not yet gone out, they contract for four [se’a per sela].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:1.hebrew: רב פפא אמר - לעולם בהלואה, דאוזיף מאה במאה ועשרין, ודקשיא לך: הלא מעל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:1.english: Rav Pappa said - Actually, [we are dealing] with a loan, where he lent one hundred [for] one hundred and twenty; and as for what was difficult to you: "Did he not commit me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property]?"

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:2.hebrew: באבני בנין - עסקינן שהלוה הגזבר מהן להדיוט, דאין בהן מעילה, ואין על הגזבר לשלם, אלא שליח בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:2.english: With building stones - We are dealing [with a case] where the treasurer lent some of them to a commoner, for there is no misuse of consecrated property in them, and the treasurer is not required to pay; rather, he is merely an agent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:3.hebrew: דאמר שמואל בונין בחול - כשהן בונין בניני הקדש, לא היו קונין האבנים והטיט ממעות הקדש, כדי שלא יבואו האומנין והעם לידי מעילה אם ישבו עליהם או אם יהנו מהם; אלא לוקחין בהקפה, והרי הן חול עד שיבנו בחומה. ומשהן בנויות בחומה, נותנין מעות הקדש ולוקחין אותן, והוא הקדשן. או אם התנדב אדם אבנים, נותנן לבנאי ואינו קורא שם הקדש עליהן עד שיתננו בבנין. הלכך, לא מעל הגזבר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:7:3.english: As Shmuel said: One builds with non-sacred [materials] - When they would build consecrated structures, they would not purchase the stones and the mortar with consecrated money, so that the craftsmen and the people would not come to [commit] misuse of consecrated property if they sat on them or if they derived benefit from them; rather, they would buy [them] on credit, and they remain non-sacred until they are built into the wall. And once they are built into the wall, they pay [with] consecrated money and acquire them, and that is their consecration. Alternatively, if a person donated stones, he gives them to the builder and does not declare a consecrated status upon them until he places them in the building. Therefore, the [Temple] treasurer has not committed misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 57b:8:1.english: For any matter of trespass - The end of the verse speaks of one who makes a claim of a thief [that the item was stolen], or of the thief himself.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:10:1.hebrew: רעהו ולא של הקדש - ובריש מרובה (ב"ק דף עו.) ממעט מוגונב מבית האיש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:10:1.english: "His neighbor, and not [property] of the Temple treasury" - And at the beginning of [the chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 76a), [the Gemara] excludes [consecrated property] from [the verse], "and it is stolen from the house of the man."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:12:1.hebrew: שומר חנם אינו נשבע - נראה דהוא הדין דאינו משלם, דאפילו שומר שכר אם פשע נראה דלא משלם, מדפריך לקמן (בבא מציעא דף נח.) "מהשוכר פועל לשמור כו'" ולא משני "כשפשע"; והיינו טעמא דמכל דין הפרשה אמעיטו. והא דלא קתני "אינו משלם", דהוי רבותא טפי, משום דעיקרה בשבועות פרק הדיינים (שבועות דף מב:), ונסבה אגררה דהתם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:12:1.english: An unpaid bailee does not take an oath - It appears that the same law applies, that he does not pay — for even a paid bailee, if he was negligent, it appears that he does not pay — from [the fact] that [the Gemara] raises a difficulty later (Bava Metzia 58a) from [the case of] "one who hires a worker to guard, etc." and does not answer "[that refers to] when he was negligent"; and the reason is that they were excluded from the entire law of the passage. And [the reason] that [the Mishnah] does not teach "he does not pay," which would be a greater novelty, is because its primary [source] is in Shevuot, in the chapter [entitled] HaDayanim (Shevuot 42b), and [the Mishnah here] brought it incidentally from there.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:12:2.hebrew: כי יתן איש אל רעהו כלל - בריש ג' מינים (נזיר ד' לה.) דריש בפרט וכלל ופרט, ובת"כ דריש בכלל ופרט לחודא. ונראה דכל הני כללי ופרטי אסמכתא, דבמרובה דרשינן מעל חמור שור ושה: חד למעוטי עבדים, וחד למעוטי קרקעות, וחד לשטרות, בין מכפל בין משבועה. והשתא אתי שפיר, דכסף או כלים דרשינן פרק שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף לט: ושם ד"ה מה): מה כלים שנים, אף כסף שנים; מה כסף דבר חשוב כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:12:2.english: "When a man delivers to his neighbor" [is] a generalization - At the beginning of [the chapter] Sheloshah Minim (Nazir 35a), [the Gemara] expounds [this passage] using a detail, generalization, and detail, whereas in Torat Kohanim it expounds [it] using a generalization and detail alone. And it appears that all these generalizations and details are [merely] an asmakhta [a scriptural support], for in [the chapter] Merubbah we expound from "for a donkey, an ox, or a sheep": one [term comes] to exclude slaves, one to exclude land, and one [to exclude] documents — both from double payment and from an oath. And now it works out well, for [the phrase] "money or vessels" we expound in the chapter Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 39b, and there, s.v. Mah): just as "vessels" [means] two, so too "money" [means] two; just as "money" [is] an item of value, etc.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:1:1.hebrew: דאפילו כל שהוא חוזר - ודוקא הקדשות, אבל קרקעות עד פלגא אינו חוזר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:1:1.english: "That even [for] any minimal amount, one may retract" - And [this applies] specifically [to] consecrated items, but [with regard to] land, up to half [its value], one does not retract.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:4:1.hebrew: בשלמא בהדיוט זה חומר ותו לא - פי': זהו חדוש שהדיוט חומר. אבל בהקדש, "זה חומר" בתמיה; פי': מה חידוש הוא שמצאנו חומר בהקדש מבהדיוט? ולא גרסינן "תו לא", שהרי אף בהדיוט איכא טובא: שומר חנם אינו נשבע, וכל הנך דמתניתין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:4:1.english: Granted, regarding a layman['s property], "this is a stringency, and nothing further" - Explanation: This is a novelty, that a layman['s property] has a stringency [over consecrated property]. But regarding consecrated property, "this is a stringency" [is said] as a rhetorical question — explanation: what novelty is it that we have found a stringency in consecrated property over a layman['s property]? And we do not read [the words] "and nothing further" [in the Gemara], for even regarding a layman['s property] there are many [stringencies]: an unpaid bailee does not take an oath [for consecrated property], and all those [cases] of our Mishnah.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:5:1.hebrew: כיון דמעל הגזבר נפקא להו לחולין - ולא מצי למימר דאוזפיה במזיד, דלא נפקא לחולין, דא"כ ליכא אגר נטר, כיון שהלוה אסור להשתמש בהם, דלא זכה בהם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:5:1.english: Once the treasurer committed misuse, they become non-sacred - And one cannot say that he lent [the coins] to him intentionally, in which case they do not become non-sacred, because if so, there is no "reward for waiting" [i.e., interest], since the borrower is forbidden to use them, as he did not acquire them.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:6:1.hebrew: לספק סלתות מארבע ועמדו משלש - תימה, היכי מיירי? אי יצא השער, או לא יצא השער ויש לו — א"כ בהדיוט נמי שרי! ואי דלא יצא השער וגם אין לו, על מה מחלל מעות הקדש? וליכא למימר שיחלל על פרוטה, דהא אע"ג שזהו ריוח הקדש שמתנה לתת ארבע סאין בסלע להקדש כל השנה, כיון דבשעת חלול מחלל על דבר שאינו שוה — זהו זילותא; דאם לא כן, אמאי הדר ביה ממאי דאוקי דאוזיף במאה כו'? ומזה הטעם נמי אין לומר לב ב"ד מתנה עליהם להתחלל בשביל ריוח הקדש, דא"כ בחנם חזר בו משנויא קמא. וי"ל: כגון שהתנדב אדם לתת ק' סלעים ולא הקדישם עדיין, ונתנם לנחתום כדי לתת להקדש ארבע סאין בכל סלע, ויצא השער של לקוטות; אבל לא יצא השער כלל — אסור, דלמא אתי לאחלופי בהדיוט, ולכך נקט: "ועמדו אחר כך משלש". וכן בזוזי, אם נתן ק' זוזי לאדם שיחזיר להקדש מאה ועשרים — אסור, דאפילו מדאורייתא נראה דאסור, דחשיב כאילו מקבל מלוה עצמו, כמו (קדושין דף ז.): "תן מנה לפלוני ואקדש אני לך", דמקודשת מדין ערב, דחשוב כאילו קבלה ממנו. והא דשרי בסמוך דאוזיף אבנים במאה ועשרים — היינו שהגזבר עצמו נותנן, וגם אבנים הם, דמוכחא מילתא שהם של הקדש; אבל דרך מקח וממכר שנתן על הסלתות, וגם יצא השער של לקוטות, שרי להקדש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 57b:6:1.english: To supply fine flour at four and they stood at three - [This is] puzzling: how is [the Gemara] speaking? If the market price has gone out, or [if] the market price has not gone out but he has [it in his possession] — if so, for a layman too it is permitted! And if [it is a case] where the market price has not gone out and he also does not have [it], onto what does he deconsecrate the consecrated money? And one cannot say that he deconsecrates [it] onto a perutah, for even though this is a profit for the Temple treasury — as he stipulates to give four se'ah per sela to the Temple treasury all year — since at the time of deconsecration he deconsecrates onto something that is not worth [that amount], this is a degradation [of consecrated property]; for if not so, why did [the Gemara] retract from what it had established [earlier], that [the treasurer] lent [a hundred] for [a hundred and twenty], etc.? And for this reason too, one cannot say that the court's heart stipulates regarding them to be deconsecrated for the sake of the Temple's profit, for if so, for naught did it retract from the first answer. And one can answer: [It is a case] such as where a person pledged to give one hundred sela'im and has not yet consecrated them, and he gave them to a baker in order to give the Temple treasury four se'ah for each sela, and the market price of gleaners [lekutot] had gone out; but [if] no market price had gone out at all, it is forbidden, lest one come to confuse [it] with [a transaction of] a layman, and therefore [the baraita] stated "and afterward they stood at three." And similarly with zuzim: if one gave one hundred zuzim to a person so that he would return one hundred and twenty to the Temple treasury, it is forbidden, for even by Torah law it appears that it is forbidden, since it is considered as if the lender himself receives [it], just like (Kiddushin 7a): "Give a maneh to So-and-so, and I will become betrothed to you," where she is betrothed by the law of a guarantor, for it is considered as if she received [it] from him. And that which [the Gemara] permits immediately following, where [the treasurer] lent stones for one hundred and twenty, that is because the treasurer himself gives them, and also they are stones, so that the matter is evident that they belong to the Temple treasury; whereas by way of buying and selling, where he gave [money] for fine flour, and also the market price of lekutot had gone out, it is permitted for the Temple treasury.
